This paper focuses on relay-assisted topology optimization to accelerate the convergence of distributed consensus algorithms over weakly connected networks. We study optimal control problems governed by a system of semilinear reaction-diffusion equations. We consider the localization and removal of a stationary omnidirectional radio source using a mobile sensor with bounded bearing errors and an unknown reception radius within known bounds.
